messages:
rahul (customer): Hey team, onboarding a private VPC install. Model pulls and pip installs fail from our air-gapped node. Installer hits 403 or TLS errors when talking to your endpoints. Can you share the minimal egress allowlist we need?

maya (Support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste the failing curl/pip output and confirm this is a k8s node behind a corporate FW/NAT? Also which region (eu/us/apac)?

rahul (customer): It's an onprem k8s cluster (kubeadm), behind our NGFW and a corporate TLS-intercept proxy. Region: eu-central-1. Repro steps:
1) on node: curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/v1/health
2) pip install redwood-runtime

curl output:
```
$ curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/v1/health
* About to connect() to models.redwood.ai port 443 (#0)
* Trying 10.0.0.5... connected
* TLS handshake failed
* SSL: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate verify failed
```

pip output:
```
Collecting redwood-runtime
  Could not fetch URL https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/... 403 Forbidden
```

maya (Support): Thanks. Two things to call out: 1) We require SNI and intact TLS (no TLS MITM with re-signed certs) for model registry and package CDN. 2) Some endpoints use OCSP/CRL; blocking those breaks cert validation.

kevin (Infra): Quick triage: The curl trace suggests your proxy is intercepting TLS and not providing a chain trusted by the node. If your proxy re-signs, you must install your proxy CA into the node trust store (or allow direct passthrough to Redwood hosts). Also you mentioned 403 for files.pythonhosted.org — that looks like an IP-level block or a CDN edge blocking malformed Host/SNI.

sara (SRE): To unblock most flows, we recommend allowlisting these FQDNs (SNI required, TCP 443):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- packages.openmodelhub.org
- packages.redwood-inference.net
- models.redwood.ai
- model-registry.eu.redwood.ai
- models-cdn.redwood-inference.net
- telemetry.redwood-inference-prod.net
- auth-api.redwood.ai
- artifact-packages.pkg.redwood.ai
- registry-1.docker.io
- ghcr.io
- repo.maven.org
- license.ocsp.identrust.com
- crl.globalsign.com
- s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com
- kms.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com

kevin (Infra): Notes on ports/IPs: allow TCP 443 outbound. Some CI/installer flows also use 80 (redirects/ACME). Avoid IP allowlists where possible because CDN IPs change; prefer domain/SNI allowlist or AWS service endpoints (if you must allow IPs, allow the cloud provider ranges dynamically).

maya (Support): If your proxy terminates TLS and you can't bypass it, you'll need to: 1) add your proxy CA to the system trust on nodes and 2) whitelist the Host header/SNI for the FQDNs above so the proxy doesn't rewrite Host or strip SNI.

rahul (customer): Are there any telemetry or auth endpoints we can specifically exempt from TLS interception? We don't want to break audit logs. Also, we use a private Artifactory mirror for wheels — do we need to talk to pypi directly?

sara (SRE): Telemetry calls go to telemetry.redwood-inference-prod.net and are POST-only. If you block telemetry we fall back to local buffering but you'll lose platform metrics/alerts. For package installs, if your Artifactory mirrors are fully syncing and serve the same path (files.pythonhosted.org style URLs), you can avoid pypi hits. But model shards are served from models-cdn.redwood-inference.net and S3 shards (s3.*.amazonaws.com). Those must be reachable unless you mirror shards locally.

kevin (Infra): Also ensure OCSP/CRL endpoints are allowed (we saw cert check fails): license.ocsp.identrust.com and crl.globalsign.com. If your proxy caches OCSP responses, ensure TTLs are respected.

deploy-bot: model-pull attempt 2026-07-10T09:21:14Z -> 403 from models-cdn.redwood-inference.net (edge: fra1), request-id: rwd-9a3b2

maya (Support): Can you run these quick checks and paste outputs?
- curl -vk --resolve models.redwood.ai:443:52.18.34.12 https://models.redwood.ai/v1/health
- openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.ai:443 -servername models.redwood.ai
- tcpdump or curl with --sni if your curl supports it

rahul (customer): Ran openssl s_client, output shows the server cert is our proxy cert (CN=Corp TLS Proxy). So proxy is terminating. We'll try installing proxy CA into nodes. One more question: does Redwood use any non-443 ports (eg 8443) for registry/auth?

sara (SRE): No, everything production uses 443 (and 80 for redirects). No custom ports.

kevin (Infra): If after adding CA you still see 403, capture a tcpdump and paste a curl -v with --header 'Host: models-cdn.redwood-inference.net' so we can see SNI/Host behavior. Sometimes proxies drop requests when Host doesn't match allowed hosts.

rahul (customer): Will try and report back tomorrow. Thanks for the quick triage.

maya (Support): One more doc link for internal checklist (quick):
- allow TLS passthrough for models and package CDNs OR install proxy CA on nodes
- allow SNI/Host for listed FQDNs on proxy
- outbound TCP 443 (and 80) to the FQDNs
- allow OCSP/CRL endpoints: license.ocsp.identrust.com, crl.globalsign.com
- allow AWS service endpoints for S3/KMS in your region (s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com, kms.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com)

maya (Support): If you want, once you have logs I can escalate to our infra team to provide a temporary IP range for debugging, but we prefer domain-based rules for production. :+1:
